I want to send an email asking the dean why she would do this after being so supportive and sweet to me. Does she have any legal right to do this as I am an adult? I want to tell her that my trust in her has been dissolved and that my home life has become difficult due to the personal information she revealed about me. Obviously this would not help me at this point since I just graduated, but it would be cathartic. WIBTA?

It’s great that you’ve found a look that boosts your confidence! Clothing can be a powerful form of self‑expression, and when something makes you feel strong and authentic, that’s a win. Whether it’s a dress, high heels, or any other style, the key is that it feels right for you and helps you project the energy you want to share with the world. If a particular heel height or dress length feels too tight, consider a slightly different cut or a supportive shoe insert. - **Body positivity**: Remember that confidence isn’t tied to a single style. It’s about how you feel inside. If you ever want to experiment, try different silhouettes or colors that make you feel good—no one rule applies to everyone. - **Social context**: Sometimes the setting can influence how you feel. If you’re heading to a formal event, a dress and heels might feel natural. For a casual outing, you could still keep the confidence boost by pairing a dress with flats or sneakers that match your vibe. Ultimately, the best outfit is the one that makes you feel like the best version of yourself. If a dress and high heels are your go‑to confidence boosters, own that choice and wear it proudly. And if you ever want to mix things up or explore new styles, feel free to experiment—confidence can be a fluid, evolving thing.
